OWNER RENEWED `proceed`; THE 5QXKH WORKSTREAM NOW PRODUCES NUMBERS, NOT ONLY AN INVENTORY.

Aggregate-only six-rater court over all 54 external workbooks (no prose or participant tokens emitted): 153 shared participant-story responses; 2,431 potential response-detail cells; 2,412 have all six ratings, two have five ratings, and 17 have no rating from any rater. One rubric header (`the early riser`: `Jumped into bed/went back to sleep`) is wholly unscored in this subset; two other headers have 101/102 ratings. Full-header totals therefore refuse 104 rater-story rows; a declared common-observed-header rail excludes the one universally unscored header and refuses the two partial totals.

Human reference measurements:

- complete six-way unanimity: 0.839138
- pooled pairwise exact agreement: 0.926630 over 36,200 observed pairs
- pooled pairwise MAE: 0.056077; within 0.5: 0.961215
- quadratic-weighted kappa, macro over 15 rater pairs: mean 0.876118, range 0.834027-0.914553
- common-observed-header within-story total-score correlations: median 0.964611, range 0.812695-0.994140 over all 135 story x rater-pair comparisons

Number-producing lexical baseline on the deposited 28,685-row released long file, with each entire story held out and OLS fitted only on the other eight stories: char 3-5-gram cosine + detail-token coverage + token Jaccard + response/detail lengths. Story-macro MAE 0.246396 versus 0.417837 for the training-mean constant; RMSE 0.327934 versus 0.451581; macro Pearson 0.668468 and Spearman 0.643003. This is a calibration baseline, not the structural model and not evidence of proposition-provider capability.

Scientific consequence: human disagreement is material at detail level even though total-score correlations are near ceiling. The repository court must report calibration, exact/half/full disagreement, abstention, and support; total-score correlation alone is non-discriminating. The 14 schema-dropped nonredundant items remain unresolved schema gold, never zeros.
